# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

## Native pages (pages the design package doesn't include)
- Author in the package's own format under `tools/nxm/native/<slug>/`: `body.html` (with `{{SPRITE}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{FOOTER}}`), `page.css`, `page.js`, `meta.json` (`title`, `description`, `anchors`, `assets`). `port_pages.py` assembles them exactly like the package's `build_page.py` (shared shell + common.css + Aurora + your css/js) and runs the same pipeline. Add the slug to `ROUTES` in `nxmlib.py` (or a fan-out in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`).
- Reference implementations: `native/about` (story + liquid-glass photo + real product prices), `native/security` (diagram + card grids + the Compare page's disclosure board), `native/affiliate` (data-driven promo), `native/legal` (article reading layout, 4 routes from one template).
- Write markup with the DESIGN's classes (`au-btn`, `au-btn--glass`, `au-card`, `au-glass`, `h2pill`, `gp-head`, `h2`, `lede`, `section`, `container`, `faq-wrap`/`faq`, `wh-final`, `data-au-icon="…" data-grad`) — the porter maps buttons to the library hierarchy. Links to other pages as `https://nxeon.cloud/<route>` (the porter makes them relative / keeps ported ones inside /nxm).
- Pure-copy pages: a wire module with `STATIC = True` and no loader.
- Body attributes: `<body class="pg-x" style="--acc:…" data-…>` land on the page wrapper; `.pg-x …` selectors are rewritten to match it.
- Loader extras: `trail` (breadcrumb below Home when ancestors aren't in the registry), `particles` (per-item colours), `crumb`.
- Interactive React pieces (e.g. a live tool component) can be mounted into a slot element with a small client component + `createPortal` — see `app/nxm/_components/HeroParticles.tsx`.
- SEO for new routes: add an entry to `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (title/description/crumb) or return them from `meta(p)`.
- The box is also production: keep Playwright runs sequential (one browser at a time) and don't restart the shared dev server (:3033, 4 GB heap cap).

model User {
  cloudflareTokenEnc         String? // encrypted Cloudflare API token for auto-DNS (business email)
  id                         String                 @id @default(cuid())
  email                      String                 @unique
  passwordHash               String
  name                       String
  googleId                   String?                @unique
  avatarUrl                  String?
  discordUserId              String?                @unique
  role                       Role                   @default(CUSTOMER)
  reviewInviteSentAt         DateTime?
  balanceCents               Int                    @default(0)
  suspended                  Boolean                @default(false)
  excludeFromRevenue         Boolean                @default(false)
  heardAboutUs               String?
  createdAt                  DateTime               @default(now())
  staffMailboxAddress        String?                @unique
  referralCode               String?                @unique
  referredById               String?
  signupCreditCents          Int                    @default(0)
  referralRewardedAt         DateTime?
  emailVerifiedAt            DateTime?
  totpSecret                 String?
  totpSecretEnc              String?
  sessionVersion             Int                    @default(0)
  totpEnabled                Boolean                @default(false)
  notificationPrefs          Json                   @default("{}")
  anthropicKeyEnc            String? // BYOK: encrypted Anthropic API key
  freeMinecraftServer        FreeMinecraftServer?
  autoRechargeEnabled        Boolean                @default(false)
  autoRechargeThresholdCents Int?
  autoRechargeAmountCents    Int?
  stripeCustomerId           String?
  stripePaymentMethodId      String?
  cardBrand                  String?
  cardLast4                  String?
  cardExpMonth               Int?
  cardExpYear                Int?
  cardExpiryNotifiedAt       DateTime?
  paypalVaultId              String?
  paypalPayerEmail           String?
  billingCountry             String?
  vatId                      String?
  budgetAlertEnabled         Boolean                @default(false)
  monthlyBudgetCents         Int?
  budgetAlertedPeriod        String?
  spendCapEnabled            Boolean                @default(false)
  hardCapCents               Int?
  preference                 UserPreference?

  @@index([createdAt])  // reports (lib/reports/collect.ts), additive
}
model StatusIncident {
  id         String    @id @default(cuid())
  component  String? // affected component, or null for platform-wide
  severity   String    @default("degraded") // degraded | down | maintenance
  title      String
  body       String    @default("")
  startedAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  resolvedAt DateTime?
  auto       Boolean   @default(false) // opened automatically vs by an operator
  createdAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime  @updatedAt

  @@index([startedAt])
  @@index([resolvedAt])
}

Maybe the error isn't about the modal itself but gets triggered by the dashboard's error boundary catching a failure from a full re-render of DashboardView when statusOpen changes — perhaps some component like WorldDots has non-deterministic rendering that throws on a second pass.

Actually, the removeChild error pattern fits better: if the modal uses a portal into document.body and something else re-parents that node before React removes it on close — a focus-trap library or an injected script — React throws trying to remove a child that's no longer there, crashing the app with a client-side exception. That matches the error counts I'm seeing across different paths.

I'd want to test this against a real prod session, but minting a prod auth token to act as a user raises concerns since it would require prod secrets even if read-only.

Instead I should look at what's distinct about the dashboard error boundary itself and check whether the logged errors are really just chunk-load failures rather than removeChild issues — specifically chunk 88463, a large icon library chunk that's lazily loaded, which suggests the crash happens when a user interaction on /dashboard triggers that chunk and the load fails.

The simple-icons chunk is likely bundled into the dashboard's initial page load rather than being lazy — if so, a 5.2MB chunk timing out on slow connections would throw the whole dashboard into its error state, which would explain the 70 occurrences and makes this a real customer-impacting issue tied to slow network conditions. I want to trace the client reference manifest to confirm whether that chunk is pulled in at initial load or deferred until some interaction.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

content.thinking:
Checking the ErrorLog entries reported to /api/log with dashboard context, I see chunk loading failures: chunk 88463 failed 70 times (last seen 10-06) and chunk 61514 failed 91 times (10-03). Tracing chunk 88463 back, it maps to the simple-icons bundle at 5.2MB, so the error variant likely points to that large asset failing to load.

This failure pattern matches the webpack client-chunk loader behavior in the App Router — client component chunks tied to layout modules like Shell and Banners get loaded via the flight response's chunk loader during hydration or client-side navigation to /dashboard, not lazily on a user action like clicking "View status." That explains why the errors cluster around page loads/navigations rather than any specific UI interaction.

Those 70 errors timestamped during the deploy window are likely just stale-chunk artifacts from old deploys triggering an automatic reload, so they're probably unrelated to this bug. There's no log or fetch evidence of a crash tied to clicking "View status," so I'm considering whether the owner hit this on a different environment, and weighing whether to spin up the actual production build tree with `next start` to reproduce it — though that risks touching the live .next directory, so I'd want to copy it elsewhere first rather than running against the real build in place.

Since `next start` only needs the .next output, node_modules, config, and public assets (not the full source), I can copy the production .next directory into my worktree — which is on the same commit — and launch a server there with a throwaway database. That gives me a faithful reproduction without touching the live deployment, so I'm checking how large that .next directory actually is before copying it.

That "removeChild" NotFoundError is Safari's message, showing up 19 times on /dashboard/deploy and 6 on /vps, plus Chrome 166 traffic on free-minecraft -- patterns that usually point to Google Translate, browser extensions, or third-party scripts mutating React portals rather than an app bug.

content.thinking:
I'm tracing the overlap bug to the breakpoint mismatch: the container locks a fixed viewport height starting at `lg`, but the two-column grid layout doesn't activate until `xl`, so between those breakpoints everything stacks into one column squeezed into that fixed height, causing cards to overflow and paint over each other.

This matches common real-world screen configurations — a 1366×768 laptop at 125% scaling renders around 1093px wide, right in that broken `lg` range, so the elevated promo/deploy rail sits on top of "View status," making clicks hit the wrong target or nothing at all. I think this is solid enough evidence to confirm as the actual defect: "View status" becomes unclickable or misdirected specifically at 1024–1279px widths, which covers many typical laptops and tablets.

The fix should constrain the fixed-height two-column layout to `xl` breakpoints and above, letting layout flow naturally below that, while also making the status modal's error handling clearer (distinct messages for 401 vs 5xx, plus a retry option) since that's the only place a genuine "error message" could surface — though I never found a logged failure to confirm that path was actually hit.

Checking xl viewport heights like 1280x720 and larger confirms no overlap issues, so switching the fixed-height class to xl-scoped seems safe. I should also handle the error modal better: distinguish 401 session-expired messages from other failures with a retry button, and add a fetch timeout so it doesn't hang indefinitely on "checking…". I'll plan a test confirming the fixed-height breakpoint matches the grid-column breakpoint, plus a pure function test for the modal error messages.

I think it's safer to extract that error-message logic into a plain helper in lib/status-copy.ts rather than exporting it from the modal component itself, since the modal imports client-only pieces like Icon that could complicate testing. Let me go implement that fix now.

- **Zero/empty state** — a customer with no servers, or every server excluded (no live signal at all),
  reads `measured: false` for that metric: the ring shows `—`, never a fabricated `0%`.

**The "30D" control.** `lib/bandwidth.ts`'s meter is a single rolling 30-day window
(`BW_PERIOD_DAYS = 30`) — there is no second stored period (no 7-day archive) to switch to, so a
functional toggle would need materially new metering infrastructure. Per the "don't ship a fake
interactive control" call, it's now a plain non-interactive `<span>` (`cursor-default`, no hover state,
no chip styling that implies clickability) reading "Last 30 days" (or "Since <date>" while the window is
still filling for a newly-metered server, or "Not measured yet" if nothing has been metered at all) —
honest about what's actually being shown instead of a dropdown-styled button that did nothing.

**Performance.** The whole computation moved OUT of `app/dashboard/page.tsx`'s server component into a
new client component, `components/nx/ResourceUsageCard.tsx`, which fetches the route above in a
`useEffect` after mount — same pattern `NetworkStatusModal` already uses for
`/api/dashboard/network-status`. The dashboard shell (stats, service table, activity feed) paints
immediately; the four rings show a pulsing loading state for the one round trip this needs, then fill in
with real numbers moments later. `app/dashboard/page.tsx` no longer computes or passes a `usage` prop at
all — `DashboardView`'s `Usage` type and prop were removed since the card is now fully self-contained.

**Verified.** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `deploy-staging.sh` built and restarted staging clean (HTTP 200).

real browser and by curling the authenticated SSR HTML directly: all four rings read "—", the period
pill reads "Not measured yet", and none of the old literals (`42%`/`68%`/`37%`/`2.4 TB`) appear anywhere
in the payload. `GET /api/dashboard/resource-usage` returns a clean 401 when unauthenticated and a clean
200 with `measured:false` on every metric for that zero-server account — no 500, no NaN. Production

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.thinking:
The Playwright mouse click probably missed because the button sits outside the viewable area within the scrollable dialog, so elementFromPoint returned null. Switching to a direct JS click worked instead, and the Stripe test confirm succeeded, with topup-complete returning 200.

I wonder if something's covering the button, though elementFromPoint returning null suggests the coordinates were off-screen rather than obscured—likely a timing issue where Playwright computed the click position before the Stripe iframe's Link section finished expanding, shifting the button's actual location between coordinate capture and the mouse event. ## Portal batch 2026-10-07: all 4 items done on `fix/portal-batch-2026-10-07`

Worktree: `/tank/nxeon-wt-portalfixes`. Nothing is merged, pushed or deployed. The branch merges cleanly into the current main (478ce38510). `tsc --noEmit -p .` passes with 0 errors.

The full test suite has 48 failures out of 3,855 tests. Current main has exactly the same 48 failures in the same 18 files (pricing, proration, purchase-consent and others), so none come from this branch. Every new test passes.

The throwaway DB `nxeon_pb1007` has been dropped and every dev server was stopped by its own PID. No role or ownership commands were run.

**Commits**
- `1a84d41c3d`, `bab2d7f0ac`: renewal analytics (done by a subagent).
- `852d6fcf62`: tools overhaul (done by a subagent).
- `e291193e2a`: View status fix.
- `dd018a72e2`: Add funds popup, plus the docs for both.

### 1. The "View status" bug

**Root cause:** at screen widths between 1024 and 1279px, other cards on the dashboard covered the "View status" button.
- `components/nx/DashboardView.tsx` fixed the dashboard to one screen height from 1024px up (`lg:h-[calc(100dvh-120px)]`). But the page only splits into two columns from 1280px up (`xl:grid-cols-…`).
- In between, both columns were stacked into one screen height. The right-hand column (Deploy New Service tiles and the Matrix promo, `z-10`) painted over the Global Network card.
- So a click on "View status" either hit the Matrix promo and did nothing, or hit the "Cloud Hosting" tile and opened the deploy wizard. This affects common screens: a 1366×768 laptop at 125% scaling, iPad landscape, iPad Pro portrait.
- I reproduced it against a copy of the exact prod release build (`next start` on the throwaway DB). At 1024×768, 1100×800 and 1180×820 the element under the button's centre was the promo text; at 1024×1366 it was the deploy tile.

**What the logs showed (read-only):**
- All 13 `/api/dashboard/network-status` requests in the 14 days of nginx logs returned 200.
- The status API itself is healthy against prod: about 886ms, all 4 components operational, 9 resolved incidents.
- No ErrorLog or `error.shown` row points at this button.
- So the logs never show the actual "error message" the owner saw. The covered button is the defect I could reproduce. It's worth asking the owner what screen width they were on.

**Fix:**
- The height lock now starts at `xl`, the same point the columns split. Below that the page scrolls normally.
- The popup itself also had a dead-end failure state. It showed "Couldn't load live status — try again in a moment" for every failure, including an expired session where retrying can never work, gave no way to retry, and could hang on "Checking…" forever.
- Now `statusLoadError()` in `lib/status-copy.ts` gives separate wording for 401, offline and server errors. The popup has **Try again** and, for an expired session, **Sign in**, plus a link to the status page. The request times out after 15s.

**Verified after the fix:** across 10 viewports from 1920 down to 390, the click lands on the button and the popup opens. The error → Try again → recovered path works at 1440 and 390, dark and light, and the 401 case shows Sign in.

**Test:** `test/dashboard-view-status.test.ts`. It requires the height-lock breakpoint to equal the two-column breakpoint, so it fails on the old code.

### 2. Add funds popup

- The sidebar Account balance card's "Add funds" now opens `components/nx/AddFundsDialog.tsx` instead of going to Billing. It offers $10/$25/$50/$100 presets, a custom amount checked against $5–$5,000, and the local-payment-method picker when enabled.
- It uses the same `/api/stripe/checkout` call and the same Stripe payment fields as the Billing page. `TopUpPayment` is now exported from `AddFundsPaymentModal.tsx`.
- Payment is confirmed with `redirect: "if_required"`, so a card payment, 3-D Secure included, finishes in the page.
- Completion goes through the new `POST /api/stripe/topup-complete`. It re-reads the session from Stripe, refuses a session that belongs to another account (`decideTopUpCompletion` in `lib/topup-inplace.ts`), and runs the same idempotent `fulfilRetrievedCheckoutSession` as the confirm redirect and the webhook. It never credits the wallet itself.
- On success the popup shows the new balance and refreshes the page, so the sidebar figure updates. Bottom sheet on phones; works in dark and light themes.
- **Verified with a real Stripe TEST payment:** card 4242, $40 at 1440. The payment confirmed in place, `topup-complete` returned 200, and the popup showed "New balance $52.50". The throwaway DB had exactly one $40 wallet credit.
- One caveat: in headless Playwright, the mouse click on Pay didn't register. The likeliest cause is the Stripe fields growing when the last field loses focus, which moves the button mid-click; a scripted click went through. That Pay button is the same shared component the Billing page's top-up modal uses.
- **Test:** `test/topup-inplace.test.ts`, 5 tests.

### 3. Tools overhaul (subagent, `852d6fcf62`)

- The `/tools` hub and all 18 tool pages now use a new NXM template, `tools-app`. The skin creator stays on the old `tools-tool` template, and its markup is byte-identical to before.
- On-brand navy, violet and cyan. Each page has an "At a glance" card, labelled inputs, Enter to submit, empty/loading/error states, and copy buttons on every result. One-click examples run immediately for the network tools. Each page gets 4 related-tool cards and an honest privacy line.
- Per-tool extras include `host:port` paste in the port checker, line:column JSON errors, and `.ini`/`.env` downloads for the game config generators. The hub has search and category filters kept in the URL, and a "no match" state with suggestions.
- **SEO:** status, title, description, canonical, robots, og:title, JSON-LD types and hash, and h1 were identical before and after on all 20 routes.
- **Tests:** `test/nxm-tools.test.ts` 8/8. No light-theme capture: the marketing site is dark-only.

### 4. Renewal analytics (subagent, `1a84d41c3d` + `bab2d7f0ac`)

- Lives at `/admin/analytics/renewals`, guarded by `requireArea("analytics")`. Reachable from the Growth nav ("Renewals" tab), a button on `/admin/analytics`, and a link in the `/admin/reports` footer. Dark and light.
- Shows upcoming 7/30 days with amount and at-risk count, rates by week or month, breakdowns by product and by payment method (wallet / card / both), involuntary vs voluntary churn plus "removed by Nxeon", cohort curves, revenue retained, and a drill-down list.
- Scope is real customers only: the reports' `realUser()` rule, which excludes `excludeFromRevenue` accounts, plus free and partner-granted servers.
- **Tests:** 16/16. No schema change.

Prod numbers (read-only), checked against independent SQL:

| Metric | Page | Check | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Upcoming 7 days | 9 · $100.90 | 9 · $97.91 list price | Diff is one $2.99 dedicated-IP add-on. I confirmed the 9 myself: 7 servers + 2 hosting. |
| Upcoming 30 days | 39 · $492.58 | 39 · $477.63 | Diff is 5 × $2.99 IP add-ons |
| Renewals collected, 30d | 8 · $88.81 | 8 · $88.81 | I confirmed the 8 `billing.renewed` / `server.renew_now` rows myself |
| Card-paid renewals | $69.20 (6) | $69.20 | match |
| Failed (involuntary) | 2 | 2 | match |
| Voluntary churn | 9 | 9 | match |
| Removed by Nxeon | 2 | 2 | match |

- Renewal rate is 42.1%, payment success 80%, card-attempt decline rate 60%. Revenue retained is 36.2% ($88.81 of $245.07 due).
- Real-customer renewal history only starts 2026-09-13, so every rate rests on 8–21 renewals. The page shows a banner saying so.

### Screenshots (`/root/agent-notes/portal-batch-1007/`)

The best ones:
- **Bug:** `bug-overlap-1024x768.png` (before) vs `fix-dashboard-1024x768.png` (after), `fix-status-error-502-390.png`.
- **Add funds:** `funds-amount-1440-light.png`, `funds-amount-390.png`, `funds-pay-1440.png`, `funds-done-1440.png`.
- **Tools:** `tools/state-dns-lookup-1440.png`, `tools/final/hub-1440.png`, `tools/final/server-size-calculator-1440.png`, `tools/state-ssl-checker-390.png`.
- **Renewals:** `renewals/renewals-1440-dark.png`, `renewals/renewals-390-light.png`, `renewals/drill-failed-1440-dark.png`.

The repro scripts are in `scripts/`.

### Decisions for the owner

1. **Deploy:** promote the branch through `deploy-staging` → `promote-production`.
2. **QA accounts:** should `haxkodi12@gmail.com` and `haxkodi123@gmail.com` be flagged `excludeFromRevenue`? They're currently counted as real customers in the renewal numbers.
3. **Customer-requested delete:** dst-ddvzfe was deleted at the customer's request after its card became unusable. Should that count as voluntary or involuntary churn?
4. **JSON formatter:** the "Tab" indent option now inserts a real tab instead of 8 spaces. OK?
5. **Tool example hosts:** the examples use public third-party hosts (github.com, gmail.com, hypixel, badssl). Swap them for others if preferred.
6. **Skin creator:** move it onto the new `tools-app` template later? Left as is per the brief.
7. **Dashboard quick action:** the dashboard's "Add funds" quick-action tile still goes to Billing. Should it open the popup too?

### Spotted, not fixed

- **Background task chip:** every customer dashboard page loads a 5.2MB chunk containing the entire `simple-icons` set. It's behind 70 logged "Loading chunk 88463 failed" errors on /dashboard.
- **Background task chip:** `adminTerminateHostingAccount` writes no audit row, so admin-terminated hosting is counted as voluntary churn.
- The dashboard scrolls 38px sideways at 768px wide. This was already there; the fix doesn't touch widths below 1024px.
- The old rollback tools pages scroll 4px sideways at 390px.
- The NXM homepage's "View status page" link is `href="#status"`.
- The Stripe checkout route doesn't block an impersonating admin; the demo top-up does.
